thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT GPU_OOM_NODE_FLAP detected on gpu-node-77 (incident-id: INC-2026-0314-77) — multiple containers restarted despite reported headroom. Creating thread for coordination.

alex (oncall): I'm on it. Confirming scope — are we seeing user-facing 5xxs or just internal restarts?

sam (customer-success): Customer telemetry shows ~3% 500s for realtime endpoints (us-west). Several support tickets from CustomerX with timeouts in the last 12m.

maria (sre): Copy. Pushing initial diagnostics. nvidia-smi snapshot from node (11:02Z):
```
GPU 0: A100-SXM4-40GB  40GB total, 12.1GB used by processes, 27.9GB free
Processes: python(1234) python(2345) runtime(9876)
```
But kernel OOM logs indicate cuda_alloc failed with out-of-memory while headroom metric shows ~20-30GB available. Suspect fragmentation or reserved blocks not freed.

devon (eng-runtime): This matches a recent pattern: KV cache reservation spikes hold lots of small reserved blocks that don't coalesce. Runtime reports `headroom_available=27GB` but `reserved_blocks_sum=34GB` in our allocator accounting — math doesn't add up because reserved blocks are counted differently.

jasper (mlinfra): Related metrics from node-metrics: `prefetch_kv_reserve=18GB`, `slab_frag_ratio=0.46`, `spare_pool=2GB`. Also seeing rapid `reserve_claim_failures` at 11:01:40Z.

alex (oncall): Immediate mitigation options? I can drain this node but we risk triggering more scheduling pressure. Prefer lighter touch first.

devon (eng-runtime): Live mitigations to try now (low risk):
- `kubectl exec -n infra runtime-pod -- /bin/sh -c "echo 0 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches"` (try clearing host caches)
- Reduce runtime's prefetch window: update config `max_prefetch=0` for pods on node.
- Evict low-priority prefetch pods: `kubectl delete pod prefetch-* --grace-period=0`
If that fails, drain node and migrate workloads.

maria (sre): Running `kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-77 -o wide` now. Found 3 prefetch pods + 12 serving pods. I'll evict prefetch first.

ops-bot: evict job queued: deleting 3 pods prefetch-ctx-{a,b,c}.

maria (sre): Prefetch pods removed. Watching allocator logs.

devon (eng-runtime): After evict: allocator trace shows `reserved_blocks_count` dropping from 1642 -> 628, but `contiguous_free_runs` still fragmented. Triggering runtime GC: `curl -X POST http://runtime-admin:8080/admin/gc?level=soft`

maria (sre): GC initiated. Kernel logs show some reclaimed pages but then `cudaMalloc` still fails for one large alloc (11.5GB). Runtime is falling back to container restart in two pods.

alex (oncall): We should failover traffic off this node. Initiating cordon and drain to prevent new assignments, then scale routing to us-east fallback pool.

devon (eng-runtime): Agree. Also propose an automated long-term mitigation: change allocator to prefer contiguous allocation by size class and add a delayed coalescer at 1m intervals. I'll open a patch, but that's not immediate.

jasper (mlinfra): Routing change done: `traffic-router` set to decrease weight for us-west-zone-1 by 60% and ramp up dedicated-pool-us-west-2 for critical customers.

sam (customer-success): Notifying CustomerX with status update: "We detected GPU memory fragmentation causing restarts; traffic rerouted to alternative pool; some requests may see <5% elevated errors during mitigation. Investigating full root cause."

maria (sre): Node cordoned. Starting drain; will forcibly evict remaining serving pods if they don't terminate in 30s.

devon (eng-runtime): Quick workaround roll: deploying runtime config v2026.03.14-hotfix that reduces `kv_cache_reserve_size` from 16GB -> 4GB for new allocs. Rolling to 20% of serving pods (canary) now: `kubectl set env deployment/runtime --env KV_CACHE_RESERVE=4G --record`

maria (sre): Canary applied to 3 pods not on the drained node. Monitoring OOM events.

incidents-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood/workflows/oom-fragmentation-runbook — added incident timeline entry.

alex (oncall): Summary of actions so far: 1) evicted prefetch pods 2) triggered runtime GC 3) cordoned/drained node 4) rerouted traffic 5) applied kv_cache hotfix canary. Customer impact: CustomerX partial timeouts, global 500 spike ~3% (being mitigated).

jasper (mlinfra): Observing reduced 500s in canary region. Node gpu-node-77 still shows one stubborn pod restart but no new OOMs post-evict.

maria (sre): Collecting heap/allocator dumps and uploading to /incident/INC-2026-0314-77/artifacts.

devon (eng-runtime): I'll own postmortem to explain allocator accounting mismatch (headroom vs reserved_blocks). Assigning action items: allocator coalescer change, add metric `contiguous_free_bytes`, and a prefetch rate-limit. Git issue created: RDW-alloc-1219.

alex (oncall): Handoff: I'm signing out in 30m. Devon will take lead for the next 12h for RCA and customer comms. @devon you're the incident lead now.

devon (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. I'll update this thread with RCA summary, timeline, and the follow-up postmortem actions once GC traces and dumps are analyzed.

sam (customer-success): I'll follow up with CustomerX and share temporary mitigations.

alex (oncall): Thanks all. Marking incident as "mitigated" for now, but leaving thread open for RCA. :white_check_mark:
